Monthly GPRi
Gross Potential Rent — max rent if every unit were occupied at its listed rate.
Source: RM scheduled rent charges (/RecurringCharges)
—
—
NOI Margini
NOI Margin — NOI ÷ income. Older multifamily: ~45–55%.
Source: RM P&L · Report 45
—
of collected income
Expense Ratioi
Expense Ratio — operating expenses ÷ income. ~45–50% typical for older stock.
Source: RM P&L · Report 45
—
of collected income
DSCRi
DSCR — NOI ÷ debt service. Lenders want ≥ 1.25x.
Source: RM P&L · Report 45 + GL 6230 Mortgage Interest (Report 54)
Interest only — RM carries no principal, so this reads better than a lender would score it.
—
—
Debt Servicei
Debt Service — mortgage interest paid.
Source: RM GL 6230 Mortgage Interest · Report 54 Cash Flow
Interest only — principal isn't in RM, so true P&I is higher.

Net Cash Flowi
Net After Debt — NOI − mortgage interest.
Before principal — real cash flow is lower.

CF / Unit / Moi
Cash Flow per Unit per Month — per-door profit after debt.
After mortgage interest, before principal.

Collection risk
Collections by Billing Month
Each month's charges are a fixed pile, locked when the month closes — then we track how much of that pile came in by the end of that month, the next, and the one after. A June charge paid in July counts toward June, never July. Excludes property taxes (TAX) and liquidated damages (LD). Goal ≥98%.

Underwriting

Underwrite a deal
Drop everything you have — the T12, the rent roll, the OM — in any mix and any format. Each file is sorted by what it is, with how sure we are. Several buildings? Drop each one's rent roll and T12 and they combine into one portfolio model. A finished Demo Portfolio model (.xlsx)? It joins the past deals below.

Fast facts + Excel download

Underwriting board — newest run first

Scoring model how a deal is scored out of 100 · click to edit
Each factor earns up to its weight. Change a weight or a threshold and the table on the right shows every deal's new score before you save. Saving applies to everyone, and re-scores the board, the Home tile and future PDFs.
The rest, in the same order
* house estimate — in-place cap rate is the T12 NOI divided by the price the model was run at (the price is itself NOI ÷ the purchase cap rate unless overridden), so read it as "what the model assumed", not a quoted cap rate. IRR, max price and the exit scenarios are the model's own numbers; the gap is max price minus the price run.
Claude extraction costs
Rent roll, T12 and OM are all read by Claude — this tracks what each document costs to process. Model math is pure code and costs nothing.
